newsitem.title: USA: Emery Latin American tonnage soars.
newsitem.headline: Emery Latin American tonnage soars.

text.p: Emery Worldwide, a unit of Consolidated Freightways Inc, is doing a booming business in Latin America, particularly Mexico, where it is adding flights, its top Latin American executive told Reuters this week.
"Last year, we were up 46 percent in tonnage in Mexico over 1995," Ron Young, Emery Worldwide's Miami-based vice president, Latin America said Thursday.
Emery expects the strong growth to continue, although Young declined to say by how much. "We have some ambitious targets, but we hope to meet them," he said.
Emery flies five days per week from its Dayton, Ohio hub to Mexico City and three days to Guadalajara. It added the third flight in January, Young said.
"We'll probably add a fourth very shortly," he said.

Emery serves Guadalajara's high-technology manufacturing companies. Mexico City has a strong auto business and also is showing good growth in electronics and telecommunications manufacturing, Young said.
"Northbound we have had very good response from fashion and textiles and perishables," Young said.
"We are looking to get into some logistics" in Mexico, Young said.
In the rest of Latin America, Emery acts as a freight forwarder and does not fly its own aircraft. Volumes in Latin America not counting Mexico were up 66 percent over 1995, Young said.
